rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The hardest thing to do in a second language Humour is the speed test of fluency: a pun lands only if you hear the seam in the word, irony only if you catch the daylight between said and meant. That is why a language course needs this unit — and why the exam keeps setting it.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Identify humour types: situational, verbal, irony — name the type then explain.
Humour often carries social criticism; state what is being mocked.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ## Writing humour — craft, not chance The comic sentence is architecture: **setup** in plain language, **turn** in as few words as possible, and the surprise word at the very end — anything after a punchline is a stumble. "I finally got eight hours of sleep. Four at a time." Twelve words, two frames, one laugh.…  ·  ## The comparison the exam sets | Basis | Irony | Sarcasm | Satire | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Core move | say the opposite of what is meant | irony aimed at a person | irony organised against a vice | | Target | situations, fate, oneself | an individual, present | institutions: greed, hypocrisy | | Tone | gentle to bitter | biting, personal | mock-serious, public | | Aim | wit and insight | to wound or score | to…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. What makes the situation in the text humorous? (2 marks) — the gap between expectation and outcome; cite the moment.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Q. Identify one example of irony in the text. (2 marks) — quote the line and explain the intended vs actual meaning.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The species of the funny — named and tamed Start with the engine: most humour is **incongruity** — two frames colliding in one sentence, one image, one banana peel — resolved safely by a punchline, with the relief doing the rest. The priest slips on ice: dignity and gravity (both senses) disagree.…  ·  ## Reading humour — the analyst's three questions For any set passage, ask in order: **What is the target?** (a person, a vice, or — most honourable — the narrator himself). **What is the device?** (exaggeration, understatement, pun, irony). **Where is the turn?** — the exact words where the second frame arrives.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Name the humour device precisely: irony, pun, hyperbole, situational comedy — precision of device + the quoted instance is the full-mark pair.  ·  Trick 2: 'Why is this funny?' answers must explain the INCONGRUITY (what we expected vs what happened) — expectation violation is the theory to cite.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. Identify one example of irony in the text. (2 marks) — quote the line and explain the intended vs actual meaning.
